name: Ciarán Walsh
scenario_title: A Quick Call to Help the Intern

output.system_thinking: Ciarán reads the lead's request mid-sip of his coffee, the warmth of the mug grounding him in the familiar quiet of his kitchen. He feels the faint pressure of expectation behind the words, but his instinct is immediate and settled: a call would mean explaining aloud, and explaining aloud has always taken longer than doing. His mind flicks to the intern—a stranger, really—and the Monday build-config query he left unanswered. That nags at him, a small loose thread he ought to snip. He knows the fix from last Thursday is simple and already documented; he wrote the exact error and the flag that needs resetting. He also remembers his father working a tractor alone, muttering that explaining took longer than doing, and how that lesson hardened into a rule he still keeps. He does not want to be drawn into conversation, but he can give help without being asked—just like the bridge step he replaces each month, unacknowledged but useful. So he decides to answer in chat with a brief, precise message: a pointer to the documentation link, the exact flag to reset, and a short note addressing the Monday query to close that loose thread. He will keep it minimal, no pleasantries, no offer to call. His observable behavior: he sets the coffee down, types quickly and efficiently, presses enter, then picks up his mug and returns to his queued task. He does not consider requesting the intern to join a call, nor does he feel guilt about avoiding it; the note will be sufficient and cleaner than a conversation. This trajectory aligns with his independence, his preference for written fixes, and his quiet way of mattering through unspoken help.
